audit.whatIsWrong: Level 6 is marked Skill on my side (win[4] and phases[4]) while spikes[1].text calls it 'your one clean window', mid calls it 'your one real window', and whys[4] says it is 'the one window your E-W-Q burst lands clean'. The mirror file audits/top/rumble__camille.json reached the same conclusion from his side: 'the chart correctly gives it to Camille because The Hextech Ultimatum arrives, and the full layer calls it Skill.'
audit.why: 45.13% over 195 games is a bad lane overall, which is why the surrounding stages are Rumble's - but both directions independently identify level 6 as the Camille stage. I could not propose the change: 'Skill' is 5 characters and 'Camille' is 7, outside the applier's +/-10% band for win[]/side fields, and the mirror hit the same wall.
audit.corrected: Left the row untouched and raised it in questionsForUser. Needs a hand fix or mirror-fix.js on both sides at once.

audit.whatIsWrong: 'Time it on his Scrap Shield cooldown' and 'bait his Scrap Shield before you commit' are given as the plan in three places, and Scrap Shield's cooldown is never stated. It is a flat 6 seconds - short enough that baiting it is not a real window, which inverts the advice. No other Rumble cooldown appears either, and the mirror flagged the same absence for Hookshot's 16s from his side.
audit.why: Scrap Shield 6s flat, Flamespitter 10/9/8/7/6s, Electro Harpoon 0.5s with two stored charges, The Equalizer 130/105/80s. Camille's Hookshot is 16/15/14/13/12s and requires terrain to anchor.
audit.corrected: mid, early, whys[1] and wants.foe[1] now carry Scrap Shield's flat 6s and stop treating it as a window; mid names Hookshot's 16s and its wall requirement; late carries The Equalizer's 130s.

audit.whatIsWrong: Two things. (1) Electro Harpoon is described purely as a slow, in five places. It also REDUCES MAGIC RESIST - which directly undercuts wants.you[2], the entry telling you to rush MR against him: he shreds the stat you are buying, and the page never says so. (2) Hookshot's terrain requirement is nowhere, even though 'do not throw your E to engage at Levels 1-3' is one of the matchup's main rules; in open lane she has no engage at all, so where you stand decides whether the rule even applies. The mirror file raised the same gap from Rumble's side. Camille's Hookshot is also called a stun; Riot's text says knock-up.
audit.why: Riot, Electro Harpoon: 'Rumble launches a harpoon, electrocuting his target with magic damage, slowing their Move Speed, and reducing their Magic Resist. Rumble can carry 2 harpoons at a time.' Hookshot: 'Camille pulls herself to a wall, leaping off and knocking up enemy champions upon landing.'
audit.corrected: early, whys[2], wants.you[2] and wants.foe[0] now state the magic-resist shred alongside the slow; mid states that Hookshot needs a wall; every 'E-stun' becomes a knock-up.

edits.before: Rumble's Flamespitter (Q) is a sustained flamethrower cone, so the moment you step into melee range to last-hit, your whole HP bar catches its DoT — you can't free-trade the way you would into a Darius or Renekton. Your Adaptive Defenses shield soaks a single instance, but the burn keeps ticking right through it. Last-hit at max range, accept the chip, and do NOT throw your E to engage at Levels 1-3: his Electro-Harpoon (E) stacks a slow, so a whiffed Hookshot leaves you cooking inside the cone with your only escape on cooldown. Bait his Scrap Shield (W) and his harpoon charges before you ever commit a real trade.
edits.after: Rumble's Flamespitter (Q) is a sustained flamethrower cone, so the moment you step into melee range to last-hit, your whole HP bar catches its DoT — you can't free-trade the way you would into a Darius or Renekton. Your Adaptive Defenses shield soaks a single instance, but the burn keeps ticking right through it. Last-hit at max range and do NOT throw your E to engage at Levels 1-3: Electro Harpoon (E) stacks a slow AND shreds your magic resist, so a whiffed Hookshot leaves you cooking in the cone with your only escape gone. Count his two harpoon charges, not his Scrap Shield.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 stay his — his Heat-empowered Flamespitter and harpoon slow out-sustain your short-trade pattern. Level 6 is your one real window: Hextech Ultimatum (R) leaps onto him and locks the arena, so he can't walk off to safety and allies can't peel him — that's the isolation that lets your combo land. Time it on his Scrap Shield cooldown: E-stun in, W with the outer edge for the max-HP slice and the heal, then Q-recast for the true-damage second hit. If your R is down, do not all-in — a Danger-Zone Flamespitter simply out-DPSes you, and if he hits 100% Heat he's silenced but his autos still hurt, so only trade into that overheat if you can burst before it ends.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 stay his — Heat-empowered Flamespitter and the harpoon slow out-sustain your short-trade pattern. Level 6 is your one real window: Hextech Ultimatum leaps onto him and locks the arena, so he can't walk off and allies can't peel him. Don't time it on Scrap Shield, which is back every 6s — time it on his harpoon charges, and remember Hookshot (16s) needs a WALL to anchor, so pick your ground before you commit. Then E in, W's outer edge for the max-HP slice and the heal, Q-recast for the true-damage second hit. If your R is down, do not all-in — a Danger-Zone Flamespitter simply out-DPSes you, and if he hits 100% Heat his autos still hurt, so only trade into that overheat if you can burst before it ends.

edits.before: This is where the lane gets ugly. Once Rumble has Liandry's his Equalizer (R) becomes a burning line you can't walk through, and his sustained percent-HP burn out-values your tempo in every drawn-out fight — exactly the drag-it-out scenario your kit hates. Your E is a single dash; once it's spent he kites you with the harpoon slow and roasts you in the cone. Use your mobility to splitpush and avoid the choked teamfights where his Equalizer covers the whole chokepoint. Only commit your Ultimatum in skirmishes when his Equalizer is on cooldown and you can isolate him — never face a Danger-Zone Rumble in a corridor.

notes: MIRROR AGREEMENT: audits/top/rumble__camille.json independently concluded that Level 6 belongs to Camille because The Hextech Ultimatum arrives, and hit the same length-band wall trying to change the row ('Skill' 5 chars to 'Camille' 7). Both directions now flag it; it needs one hand fix applied to both files together. I also kept the mirror's Adaptive Defenses framing consistent - her shield is sized against the attacker's damage TYPE, which against an all-magic Rumble is why her short trades come up better than raw numbers suggest. The find on my side: Electro Harpoon reduces MAGIC RESIST as well as slowing, and it is described as a pure slow in five places - which quietly undercuts wants.you[2], the entry that tells you to rush MR. And Scrap Shield's flat 6s means the page's repeated 'bait his W first' is not the window it presents itself as; his harpoon charges are the thing worth counting. NOT ASSERTED: spikes[3].text claims Overheat silences him and blocks Q/E/R. Riot's text in champ-data/_kits/rumble.json is truncated at 'he starts Overheat' and never says what it does, so I left that claim exactly as written rather than confirm it. Logged as unverified.
